title: How do group cases and written cases work, and how do you do well in them?
description: What to expect from group case exercises and written case interviews, used by the Big Four, Bain, Oliver Wyman and others, and how to stand out.
hook: Not every case is a one-to-one conversation. Many firms use group cases, where you solve a problem with other candidates, or written cases, where you read a pack and present. Both reward slightly different skills, and both can be practised.
body:
Group cases

Four to six candidates get a business problem and work on it together while assessors watch, then often present. Deloitte, EY, KPMG and some strategy firms use them.

  • Assessors watch how you work with others as much as your ideas.
  • Do: suggest a structure early, build on others' ideas, keep time, bring quieter people in, and help the group reach a recommendation.
  • Avoid: talking over people, dominating, or going silent.
  • A simple, helpful line: "Shall we agree how to split the time first, so we leave ten minutes to prepare the recommendation?"

Written cases

You receive a pack of slides or data, prepare alone for a set time, then present, sometimes on slides you make. Bain (in some offices), Oliver Wyman, L.E.K. and Monitor Deloitte use them.

  1. Skim first. Find the question and the goal before reading any detail.
  2. Pick the exhibits that matter. Not every page is useful; some are there to test your judgement.
  3. Do the key calculations and check them.
  4. Build a short story: answer first, two or three supporting points, risks, next steps.
  5. Leave time to rehearse the opening sentence.

How to practise

  • Run a group case with three or four friends; rotate who keeps time and who summarises.
  • Use BCG's downloadable written case and other official material to practise written cases against the clock.

A time plan for a 45-minute written case

  • 5 minutes: read the question and skim every page without detail.
  • 15 minutes: pick the 3 or 4 exhibits that matter and do the calculations.
  • 15 minutes: write 3 or 4 slides: recommendation, two supporting points, risks and next steps.
  • 10 minutes: check numbers and rehearse your first two sentences.

Sources

  • Simplify: Consulting case interview prep (group cases)
  • Hacking the Case Interview: Monitor Deloitte interview
  • PrepLounge: Bain (written cases)

Checked November 2026.

A worked approach to a group case

Imagine five candidates must recommend where a grocery chain should open its next store. There are three locations with different rents, footfall, competition and transport links. Propose an evaluation table before arguing for your favourite. Put expected contribution, investment, customer access, strategic fit and principal risk in the columns. Assign someone to check assumptions and someone to watch time, without monopolising the discussion.

Suppose Site A offers £1.2 million annual contribution before rent and £600,000 rent; Site B offers £900,000 before rent and £250,000 rent. Based on those figures alone, Site B delivers £650,000 after rent, versus £600,000 for A, despite A's stronger sales potential. Yet the group still needs to consider initial investment, market growth and operational feasibility before deciding.

In a written case, use the same discipline: answer first, a short comparison table, key calculations, recommendation, risks and the next test. In a group exercise, assessors can see whether you improve the team's thinking without overpowering quieter candidates. Good collaboration is observable in questions and synthesis, not just airtime.
